requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. The single code path and its tests cover every obligation.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out (all in `src/config.rs`):**
- **Unix, absolute nonempty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`:** `user_config_path_from` (688–701) uses `absolute_directory(.., "XDG_CONFIG_HOME")` and joins `habeas/config.toml`. `absolute_directory` (724–730) rejects an empty or relative value, because `PathBuf::from("").is_absolute()` is false.
- **Unix, otherwise `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`:** the `None` branch uses `required_directory(.., "HOME")?.join(".config")`.
- **Windows `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`:** the `ConfigPlatform::Windows` branch uses `required_directory(.., "APPDATA")`. `ConfigPlatform::current` (303–311) picks the platform, and `user_config_path` (683–686) feeds it the real environment.
- **`HOME` and `APPDATA` absolute and nonempty:** `required_directory` (732–744) applies the same `absolute_directory` check.
- **Failure with a diagnostic naming the variable:** `required_directory` returns an `io::Error` reading "cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path".
- **Same configuration usable across projects; location not project-relative or changed by project settings:** `user_config_path` takes no project argument and reads only environment variables. A search for other computations of the user path (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `APPDATA`, `.config/habeas`) found none. `resolve_authoring` (960–979) obtains the path from `user_config_path()`, independent of the workspace.
- **Workspace settings use `habeas.toml`:** this is covered by the cited `workspace_location`, so I did not reassess it.
- **MAY on user-local project preferences:** imposes nothing to check.

**Tests (`tests/configuration.rs`):**
- `locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` (12–66) checks these cases:
  - a valid `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`;
  - an empty or relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to `HOME/.config`;
  - Windows `APPDATA`;
  - an error when nothing is set.
- `base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty` (1466–1506) checks these cases:
  - an empty or relative `HOME` or `APPDATA` is an error whose message contains the variable name;
  - a relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falls back to an absolute `HOME`.

**Marking:** the code and tests all carry `{impl}` or `{test}` references to `requirements.configuration.user_location`. I found no unmarked implementing code and no unspecified behavior.

text: :::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
